subject: End-of-term orchestration & notice runbook — MSA + Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@atlashealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Atlas Health Procurement <procurement@atlashealth.com>, Atlas Legal <legal@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on Term & Renewal — MSA + Order Form

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team and procurement ran a quick pass and attached a redline (redlined_MSA_v3.pdf + orderform_ATLAS_v2.docx) with a few items that are blocking internal approval. High level:

- Auto-renew: We want an explicit opt-out window (30 days before renewal) and clearer notice mechanics so procurement doesn't miss the window.
- Notice window for termination for convenience: Atlas requests 60 days (we like shorter windows given internal fiscal planning).
- Refunds & unwinding: We expect pro rata refund language for prepaid services if Redwood terminates for convenience or materially downgrades service.
- Data retention/hand-off: a runbook for service transfer on termination (who will ship data, timelines, and fees).

Can you confirm Redwood's position on the above? If you can accept the 30-day opt-out window and 60-day convenience notice, we should be able to proceed to procurement sign-off quickly.

Also copied procurement/legal for visibility.

Thanks,

Sarah Lin
Head of Partnerships, Atlas Health
sarah.lin@atlashealth.com

--
Attachment: redlined_MSA_v3.pdf (PDF, 1 p redline summary)
Attachment: orderform_ATLAS_v2.docx (Word, proposed order form)

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@atlashealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Term & Renewal — MSA + Order Form

Sarah — thanks for the redlines and clear summary. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Monica (Sales Ops) to confirm feasibility and update docs. Quick read below with immediate thoughts: 

- Auto-renew / opt-out window: We usually propose a 60-day opt-out for enterprise commitments to ensure billing/ops lead time; a 30-day window is tight but may be OK if we (a) lock the final billing schedule earlier and (b) require notices to the designated procurement mailbox (procurement@atlashealth.com) and to your account team.

- Termination for convenience (TFC) notice: Redwood's standard is 90 days for Enterprise to allow capacity planning, but we can consider 60 days if the order form is for pilot or <= $75k ARR. For committed/discounted pricing we need 90 days. 

- Refunds & unwinding: We can agree to pro rata refunds for prepaid unused service when Redwood initiates termination for convenience. If the customer terminates for convenience, we generally do not provide refunds unless it's within an agreed trial or pilot. Let's confirm which party is proposing the TFC.

- Data hand-off/runbook: We can provide a 30-day export window and standard export formats. Karthik — can you add language around the service wind-down and timelines (who provides data, retention, whether there are fees) so we have something redline-ready? Monica — once we have the language we can update the order form in HubSpot and prep a DocuSign.

Propose next steps: Karthik to send a legal-sided redline by tomorrow morning, Monica will prepare an order-form variant for 60-day vs 90-day scenarios, and then we can schedule a 30-min legal alignment call if needed.

Sound good?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on Term & Renewal — MSA + Order Form (redlines attached)

Thanks Aditya / Sarah — I reviewed the redline and attached a legal draft (redlines_karthik.docx) with recommended language. Key points in the redline: 

1) Auto-renew & opt-out mechanics:
   - We can accommodate a 30-day opt-out window provided the notice requirement is strict: written notice to the designated procurement mailbox + account manager, and an explicit effective date (we process renewals on the 1st of the month after the period).
   - If Atlas requests the 30-day window, we require an earlier invoice cutoff (45 days) so finance teams can reconcile.

2) Termination for convenience (TFC):
   - Proposal: Mutual TFC with notice tiers — Orders <= $75k: 60-day notice; Orders > $75k: 90-day notice. Rationale: higher-value commitments need longer runway for resource reallocation.
   - If Redwood initiates TFC, we will provide pro rata refund for prepaid fees for the unused portion.
   - If customer initiates TFC, refunds are subject to any committed minimums or prepaid term discounts (standard commercial tradeoff).

3) Wind-down / data hand-off:
   - Add a Service Wind-down Schedule section to the MSA: timeline for export (30 days), file formats (S3-compatible export or encrypted JSON/CSV), and a hand-off acceptance sign-off. Fee for extended retention beyond 90 days to be negotiated.

4) Cure & breach language:
   - Keep a 30-day cure period for termination for cause; do not conflate with TFC.

Next steps: I recommend we mark two order-form templates in HubSpot (60-day and 90-day) and add clarifying fields for "Order Value" and "Renewal Opt-Out Email". Monica — can you create the two templates and set the default routing? Aditya — happy to hop on a 20-min call with Atlas counsel if they want to walk through the approach.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redlines_karthik.docx (Word, legal redline with suggested language)

Subject: Re: Questions on Term & Renewal — MSA + Order Form

Sarah — thanks for the quick turnaround. Operationally we can support the split templates Karthik suggested. Action items and timelines from Sales Ops: 

- I will create two order form variants in HubSpot today (labelled "Atlas - 60d TFC" and "Atlas - 90d TFC") and add a field for "Renewal Opt-Out Email" and "Order Value".
- Once Karthik confirms redline text, I will publish the appropriate order form and generate a DocuSign envelope (link will be posted to the HubSpot deal).
- Please confirm whether Atlas intends to sign the 60-day option (pilot / <= $75k), or whether this is a higher-commitment deal. If you confirm 60-day by end of day we will push the 60-day template; otherwise default is 90-day.

Proposed timeline:
- Today EOD: HubSpot templates created and DocuSign envelope prepared (pending final redline).
- Tomorrow 11:00am PT: optional 20-min alignment call (Aditya / Karthik / Atlas legal) to run through the redline and confirm final template.

I will attach the HubSpot and DocuSign links to the deal after I publish.
